ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Patient initially typed “jaw pain,” but main concern today is progressive numbness/tingling in left arm; possible trigger is recent boxing classes started a few weeks ago.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Tingling began ≈2 weeks ago, gradually worsened to numbness.
  • Intermittent jaw discomfort noted but not elaborated.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Not reported.
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia: Denied.
  • Drooling: Not reported.
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: No nasal issues; transient left-eye visual field loss ×20 min about 2 weeks ago.
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: Denied.
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: Denied.
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: Denied.
  • Neck pain/swelling: Denied.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Recent “really bad cold” ≈1 month ago lasting 2 weeks.
  • Tried massage and hot baths without relief.
  • No prior ED visits or injections for current issue.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Current medications:
  • Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  • Vitamin D supplement (dose/frequency not documented).
  • Iron supplement intermittently (dose/frequency not documented).
  • Melatonin as needed for sleep (dose/frequency not documented).
- Social context:
  • Lives independently; no mention of supervision or accompaniment.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, no respiratory distress stated.
- Mental status: Alert; no syncope or seizure activity reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Companion present: None; tele-consult alone.

Assessment:
- No acute ENT pathology identified.
- Primary impression by consulting physician: Possible neurological condition (e.g., multiple sclerosis) given unilateral arm numbness and transient monocular visual disturbance.

Plan:
- Urgent neurology referral arranged for brain imaging and further evaluation.
- No ENT-specific intervention required at present.
- Red-flag advice provided: attend emergency department if weakness progresses (e.g., involves legs), new or worsening headaches, vomiting, seizures, or visual symptoms recur/persist.
- No medications initiated; steroid therapy deferred pending neurologic assessment.
- Patient advised to monitor symptoms and seek emergency care if red-flag signs develop.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: complete allergy list; ENT physical exam findings (oropharynx, neck, otoscopy); detailed medication dosages; availability of emergency devices (e.g., auto-injector not relevant but blank).
● Internal conflicts: None identified.
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional conversational digressions but clinically usable.
